correctness.rationale: The strip removes two congruent triangular caps of Euclidean area (1-h)^2 cot(pi/n) each. The polar is conv(P_n^circ,(±1/h,0)), replacing two polar edges by triangles of area (1/h-1)tan(pi/n), yielding A_n=n sin(pi/n)cos(pi/n)-2(1-h)^2 cot(pi/n) and B_n=(n-2+2/h)tan(pi/n), hence the claimed product. Differentiation gives M_n′(h)=2 G_n(h)/h², with G_n(h)=2+(2n-6)h²+(4-2n)h³-nq and G_n′(h)=-2h[3(n-2)h-2(n-3)]. For even n>=6, G is strictly decreasing on [cos(2pi/n),1], with positive lower endpoint and negative upper endpoint; n=4 has direct quadratic M_4=8+4h-4h². Thus a unique interior maximum follows. Inserting w=1-h_n=q/2+O(q²) into the exact difference yields gain pi^4/(2n³)+O(n^-5); the regular polygon benchmark increment is 4pi^4/(3n³)+O(n^-4), giving 3/8. Independent geometric polygon/polar area and root checks corroborate several even n. No finite check is substituted for the general polar and derivative proof.

originality.rationale: Meyer–Reisner’s optimal-volume-product regular polygon result provides the external at-most-(n+2)-vertices benchmark, and shadow-system theory gives qualitative deformation framework, but neither readily supplies this exact one-strip polar-area profile and unique interior maximizer. Lin–Leng studies product-reducing vertex removal in a planar symmetric minimum setting, not the strict interior max along a prescribed clipping family. Related published 3D cube–cross-polytope Mahler interpolation and simplex difference-body profiles use other bodies. The constrained even-polygon formula and 3/8 efficiency limit remain original by checked statements, with a direct 2011 source full-text access risk.
residual_risks: Full text of Meyer–Reisner 2011 On the volume product of polygons remained inaccessible, including Oxford VPN disconnected; it may contain related explicit calculations beyond the inspected abstract.
The result is only for the prescribed strip range and even polygon orders; it is not a global theorem for arbitrary clipping, odd polygons or higher dimensions.

This is not an arbitrary slice of a table or a mere endpoint computation.
